issue_text: classForCount() downgrades a "blocking"-classified finding to "warning" (non-blocking) when its severity is not critical/high (default branch, line 424-425). This severity gate directly drives gate verdicts: OpenBlockingCount, CountByClass().Blocking, and unresolvedBlockingFrom() all route through classForCount, and every task-done/pr-ready/epic-ready gate blocks on counts.Blocking > 0. Yet NO test in the findings package exercises a "blocking" classification at medium/low severity. The whole switch could be deleted (making every "blocking" finding block regardless of severity) or widened to `!= "low"` and the entire findings package test suite stays green — silently promoting medium-severity blocking findings to gate-closing blockers.
why_real: Every findings-package test that uses classification "blocking" sets severity "high" (unsafeEval, findings_test.go:325) or "critical" (override recur test, findings_test.go:496). TestCountByClass... (findings_test.go:11) uses spec-contract/advisory/follow-up/novel — no "blocking" record at all, so classForCount's blocking branch is never hit there. Deleting lines 420-426's inner severity switch and returning "blocking" unconditionally leaves all findings tests passing. This is the exact class of gap the SISTER package explicitly closed: internal/reviewlog has a parallel isOpenBlocker() with TestOnlyCriticalAndHighSeveritiesBlock (reviewlog_test.go:511) whose own comment records the lesson — "only three of its four cases were pinned - medium had none, so widening the set from (critical|high) to != 'low' left the suite green and silently promoted every medium finding to a blocker." findings.classForCount has no equivalent enumeration.
tests_checked: findings_test.go: TestCountByClassSeparatesBlockersAdvisoriesFollowUpsAndWarnings (no blocking-class record), TestReconcileFindingsLifecycle / TestReconcileReturnsOpenFindingsForCurrentTarget / all Reconcile tests (unsafeEval => blocking+high), TestSpecContractFindingsBlockRegardlessOfSeverity (spec-contract path only), TestReconcileClosesAPendingOverrideThatWasActuallyFixed (blocking+critical). None uses blocking+medium/low. Cross-checked repo: only internal/reviewlog/reviewlog_test.go:TestOnlyCriticalAndHighSeveritiesBlock pins this rule, and it tests reviewlog's own isOpenBlocker, not findings.classForCount.

issue_text: canonicalClass() aliases "blocker" -> "spec-contract" (line 403) and "followup" -> "follow-up" (line 409), plus the ReplaceAll("_","-") normalization (line 401). These aliases are gate-affecting: a finding classified "blocker" resolves to spec-contract which classForCount always treats as blocking. But no test anywhere feeds classification "blocker", "followup", or an underscore variant. Removing the "blocker" alias makes such a finding fall to default -> "warning" -> non-blocking, and every test still passes.
why_real: Grep across all *_test.go Classification: literals yields only blocking, advisory, follow-up, spec-contract, novel, warning — never "blocker", "followup", or "spec_contract". So the alias arms of canonicalClass are unpinned: deleting `case "blocker"` (leaving only "spec-contract") or `"followup"` from line 409, or the underscore ReplaceAll, keeps the findings suite green while changing how a real "blocker"-tagged finding is counted at a gate. Lower severity than findings-1 because the canonical spellings (blocking/spec-contract) are the ones the pipeline emits; the aliases are defensive input-normalization with no coverage.
tests_checked: findings_test.go all tests (classifications used: blocking, spec-contract, advisory, follow-up, novel); override_test.go (blocking only). Repo-wide grep of Classification: literals in *_test.go confirms no "blocker"/"followup"/underscore forms are ever supplied.
